responsibility: This module implements the gccrs frontend’s semantic checking and linting layer, covering the crate analyses that validate Rust language rules after parsing and during/after HIR construction, plus a few backend-oriented diagnostics on lowered GCC trees. Its major responsibilities are split between error-checking passes under errors/ and warning-style analyses under lints/: the errors side includes early AST validation and feature gating, HIR-based enforcement of const, unsafe, mutability/readonly, and pattern-exhaustiveness rules, a full privacy subsystem that resolves visibilities, validates pub(restricted), computes reachability, and reports private-use violations, and a substantial borrow-checking subsystem that lowers functions into a dedicated Borrow-checker IR (BIR), models places and regions, collects Polonius facts, interfaces with the Polonius engine through FFI, and translates borrow-check results into source diagnostics. The lints side provides symbol-liveness and dead-code analysis over HIR as well as unused-variable-style warnings on backend declarations. Together, this module is the Rust frontend’s rule-enforcement and diagnostic-analysis stage, distinct from parsing, name/type resolution, and code generation because it focuses on legality checks, safety/privacy semantics, borrow analysis, and user-facing warnings/errors.
